svg.title: A pool buys real cores and charges a toll on every task
svg.desc: A parent process fanning work through a dashed pickle toll booth out to four child processes, each drawn with its own GIL. Bars compare worker startup at 54 ms for spawn, 43.2 ms for forkserver and 3.8 ms for fork. A crossover curve shows the pool below break-even until about 100 000 iterations of work per task, with the losing region hachured in red, and a sketch shows eight workers each spawning eleven BLAS threads onto eleven cores.
svg.text: A pool buys real cores and charges a toll on every task
pickle 100k ints: 659 us out, 1313 us in
64 tiny tasks cost 50 ms of pure overhead and return nothing.
fork is 14.2x cheaper and quietly unsafe once
you have threads. That is the whole trade.
spawn re-imports the module. Processes all the way down.
...and why is each worker's RSS the parent's?
